title: Skip disk/history validation when path normalization is a no-op
context: The guard needs to disambiguate whether a backslash in a path entry is a literal POSIX filename character or a Windows path separator, using a disk/history check. But when a path has no backslash, toPosixTarget() doesn't change it, making the expensive check redundant. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Only call namesRealEvidence (disk/history lookup) when toPosixTarget(f) actually changes the string. For entries with no backslashes, skip the validation entirely since normalization is already a no-op.
consequences: Eliminates unnecessary filesystem and git history checks for paths that don't require normalization
Accepts an edge case gap: a file deleted from history that coincidentally matches a Windows-style path in a sibling worktree now fails open (no misroute reported) instead of being disambiguated
Identical behavior for all inputs that actually need normalization—optimization is purely internal
alternatives_rejected: Always perform namesRealEvidence check regardless (original code)—wastes I/O when normalization changes nothing
Remove the check entirely—loses disambiguation capability for genuine Windows-style paths
